messages.content: We're ready to look at the April coast trip. Five nights, Thursday through Tuesday, for the two of us from Minneapolis. We're debating Savannah plus Tybee Island or Charleston plus Folly Beach, and flights plus lodging need to stay under $3,800.

I can compare them on a Thursday, April 23 departure and Tuesday, April 28 return. Before I build the two plans, do you want meaningful city time as well as beach time, or is the city mainly where you would fly and have dinner?
Meaningful city time. Probably two nights in the city and three near the beach, but I want to know whether changing hotels wastes too much of a five-night trip.

A two-and-three split is workable in both places because the coast is close. Savannah to Tybee is roughly 18 miles and typically 30-45 minutes by car; downtown Charleston to Folly Beach is about 12 miles but can take 25-50 minutes depending on traffic. The hotel change itself would consume part of Saturday: checkout, luggage handling, transportation, and waiting for the coastal room. You could preserve most of the day by leaving bags with the second hotel before check-in.
Show me realistic totals for both. We can fly out Thursday morning and come back Tuesday afternoon or evening.

Using representative late-April economy fares and refundable-or-flexible lodging rates, Savannah comes out lower. MSP-SAV itineraries with one connection are about $475 per person round trip, or $950 for two. Two downtown Savannah nights at about $265 nightly plus tax are approximately $610, and three Tybee nights at about $315 nightly plus tax are approximately $1,090. Flights and lodging total about $2,650.

For Charleston, nonstop MSP-CHS service may be available on limited schedules, while the broader selection has one connection. A reasonable working fare is $430 per person, or $860 for two. Two downtown nights at about $315 nightly plus tax are approximately $725, and three Folly Beach nights at about $385 nightly plus tax are approximately $1,330. That total is about $2,915. Both fit the $3,800 ceiling, with Savannah leaving roughly $1,150 and Charleston roughly $885 before ground transportation, meals, parking, or resort fees.
What do the flight days actually look like? A cheaper plan isn't useful if Thursday disappears in airports.

A practical Savannah outbound would leave MSP around 7:00 a.m., connect in Atlanta, and reach SAV around 12:30 p.m. Including the transfer downtown, you could be at the hotel near 1:30 p.m. The return could leave SAV around 2:30 p.m. and reach MSP around 7:00 p.m. after a connection.

Charleston has the stronger flight-day possibility: a late-morning nonstop, when operating on these dates, would arrive around 2:00 p.m. Eastern. Otherwise, a one-stop itinerary leaving around 7:30 a.m. would arrive around 1:00 p.m. A nonstop return could leave in midafternoon and reach MSP before 6:00 p.m.; a connecting option would generally arrive between 7:00 and 9:00 p.m. Exact schedules and fares would need confirmation before purchase.
So Charleston might gain time even though it costs more. How much beach time would we really get with the split plans?

For either split, Thursday afternoon and Friday would be city time. On Saturday, you could check out around 9:00 a.m. and reach the beach area by 10:00 or 10:30, leave luggage, and spend the rest of the day near the water. Sunday and Monday would be full beach days. Tuesday would allow breakfast and perhaps a short walk, but not a dependable beach block once checkout and the airport transfer are included. That yields about two full beach days plus most of Saturday.

Charleston's possible nonstop saves airport time, but it does not materially add a beach day under the same two-city, three-coast split. Its advantage is a simpler travel day, especially on the return.
Could we stay in one place and avoid renting a car? Compare that honestly.

Yes, but the tradeoff differs. In Savannah, five nights downtown would be around $1,525 with tax, putting flights and lodging near $2,475. Rideshares to Tybee commonly run about $40-$65 each way before surge pricing. Two round trips could add $160-$260, and availability for the return pickup should be checked. You would gain one hotel base but spend 2-3 hours total commuting for two beach days.

In Charleston, five downtown nights would be around $1,810 with tax, putting flights and lodging near $2,670. Rideshares to Folly may be about $30-$55 each way, though traffic and surge pricing can raise that. Two beach round trips could add $120-$220. It is feasible without a rental car, but carrying beach gear and relying on a pickup after dinner are less convenient. Staying all five nights at either beach would make city visits the commute instead and would reduce the value of the first two days as a city break.
I don't love paying beach hotel rates and then commuting from downtown, but I also don't want parking charges to blow up the comparison. What would transport cost for the split?

For Savannah and Tybee, you could avoid a full-trip rental: rideshare from SAV to downtown for roughly $25-$35, downtown to Tybee for $40-$65, and Tybee to SAV for $35-$55. Allowing for local rides and variability, budget $150-$230 total. Confirm that the Tybee lodging has no mandatory parking or destination fee even if you arrive without a car.

For Charleston and Folly, comparable transfers would be about $35-$50 from CHS to downtown, $30-$55 downtown to Folly, and $35-$60 from Folly to CHS. With a few local rides, budget $145-$235. A rental car for all five days could easily reach $350-$500 before downtown and beach parking, so point-to-point rides are the cleaner fit unless you plan excursions beyond those two areas.
Add those transport allowances and any likely lodging fees. I want the comparison to be conservative, not a best-case teaser.

A conservative Savannah split budget would be: $950 flights, $1,700 lodging with tax, up to $230 for rides, and a $150 cushion for lodging fees or fare movement. Working total: $3,030, leaving about $770 under the flight-and-lodging ceiling even though I have included transport and a cushion for context.

A conservative Charleston split would be: $860 flights, $2,055 lodging with tax, up to $235 for rides, and a $200 cushion for possible destination fees or fare movement. Working total: $3,350, leaving about $450. A specific Folly property can change that quickly: a $35 nightly resort or destination fee over three nights, once taxed, would use roughly another $120. Neither estimate includes meals.
What about weather and the actual beaches in late April? We don't need swimming every day, but we want the coast to feel like the point of the trip.

Both should feel coastal, but neither guarantees warm-water swimming in late April. Typical daytime highs are in the mid-to-upper 70s, evenings can be cool, and Atlantic water is often around the upper 60s to low 70s. Tybee has a laid-back island layout, broad beach access, and a more distinct separation from Savannah. Folly has a compact beach-town center with restaurants near the sand and an easy pairing with Charleston. Weather risk is similar enough that it should not decide the trip; lodging location within walking distance of the beach matters more than a small average-temperature difference.
Which one would you choose for only five nights? We want two good city days and then to settle in near the beach, and I don't want the budget to feel tight once taxes and fees appear.

I would choose Savannah plus Tybee for this trip. The two-night Savannah and three-night Tybee split gives you the city-and-coast structure you want, nearly the same usable beach time, and roughly $300 more protection against fare or hotel changes in the conservative comparison. Tybee also makes the second half feel clearly separate from the city rather than like a day trip.

Charleston is the better choice only if the nonstop operates at favorable times and simplifying the flight days is worth the higher lodging exposure. With five nights and a firm ceiling, Savannah offers the better balance: arrive Thursday around midday, spend Thursday afternoon and all Friday in Savannah, transfer to Tybee Saturday morning, use Saturday afternoon through Monday at the coast, and return Tuesday afternoon.
Keep Savannah as the recommendation, but don't pick hotels yet. Give me the numbers and the key thing to verify next.

Recommended framework: Thursday, April 23 through Tuesday, April 28; two nights in Savannah followed by three nights on Tybee Island. Current working figures are $950 for two round-trip economy tickets, about $1,700 for lodging with tax, $150-$230 for point-to-point transportation, and a $150 contingency for fare movement or property fees. The conservative all-in planning figure is $3,030, while flights plus lodging alone are about $2,650 against the $3,800 ceiling.

The next verification should be the flight schedule, specifically whether the Savannah itinerary can leave MSP near 7:00 a.m. Thursday, arrive around 12:30 p.m., and return Tuesday afternoon without a long connection. After that, compare Tybee properties for a true walk-to-beach location and screen the final price for destination fees, cleaning fees, and minimum-stay restrictions before choosing a hotel. Nothing has been selected or booked.
